div.head: II Cn 73
div.ab: ⁊ sitte ælc wuduwe werleas XII monað, ceose syððan þæt heo sylf wylle.
And sitte ælc wuduwe werleas twelf monað, ceose siððan þæt hio silf wille.
Et sit omnis uidua sine marito XII mensibus; eligat postea, quem uelit.
Be wydewan, þæt heo sitte XII monðas ceorlæs. And sitte ælc wuduwe werleas twelf monað ⁊ ceose heo syððan þæt heo sylf wille.

And sitte ælc wuduwe werleas XII monað, ceose syððan þæt heo sylf wylle. And gif heo binnan geares fæce wer geceose, þonne þolige heo þære morgengyfe and ealra þæra æhta þe heo þurh ærran wer hæfde; and fon þa nehstan frynd to ðam landan and to þan æhtan þe heo ær hæfde.
Concerning widows, that they remain for a year without a husband. And every widow shall remain twelve months without a husband, and she shall afterwards choose what she herself desires.

And every widow shall remain without a husband for twelve months, and afterward she shall choose as she herself desires. Yet if she then chooses a husband within a year, she shall forfeit her morning gift and all the property she inherited from her previous husband; and his closest relatives shall take the land and possessions that she had hitherto held.
And each widow is to remain unmarried for 12 months; she is afterwards to choose what she herself will.
(Von der Wittwe, dass sie zwölf Monate gattenlos sitze. B) Und jede Wittwe sitze gattenlos zwölf Monate lang, (und B) wähle sie nachher, was sie selbst will.
(Of the widow, that she should remain twelve months without a husband. B) And let every widow remain without a husband for twelve months; (and, B) afterwards let her choose what she herself wishes.

morning gift: A gift, often in the form of money or land, from a newly married husband to his wife, supposedly given the morning after their first night together. The gift was considered the woman’s property and, in theory at least, was kept separate from the other aspects of the couple’s finances overseen by the husband.
